app.title: Ankle fracture classification
app.description: Answer the questions to obtain the Lauge-Hansen, Danis-Weber, AO/OTA, and Bartonicek classification

hero.title: Four ankle fracture classifications from one set of answers.
hero.lede: Anklyze follows a single decision tree drawn by orthopedic surgeons. Answer what you see on the radiograph and it returns Lauge-Hansen, Danis-Weber, AO/OTA and Bartonicek together.
hero.secondary: See how a result is reached

example.caption: Example: an isolated lateral malleolus fracture, read through the tree. N/C means the system does not apply.

answer.title: Answer what you see
answer.body: The questions follow the fracture: which malleoli are involved, the level of the fibular fracture, the pattern of the trace. Number keys answer, and nothing is asked that the tree does not need.

narrow.title: The tree narrows
narrow.body: Each answer selects the next question. The path you took stays on screen, so a colleague can check how the result was reached.

result.title: One result in four systems
result.body: The end of the path carries the classification in all four systems. When a system does not apply to the fracture, the result says so instead of forcing a code.

systems.title: The four systems
systems.lede: Each system describes the same fracture from a different angle. Anklyze reports them side by side, so none has to be worked out separately.
systems.laugeHansen: Mechanism of injury: the position of the foot and the direction of the deforming force.
systems.danisWeber: Level of the fibular fracture relative to the syndesmosis.
systems.aoota: Alphanumeric code for bone, segment, type and group.
systems.bartonicek: Morphology of the posterior malleolus fragment.

studies.title: Built for reliability studies
studies.lede: Researchers publish cases with their imaging, invite raters to classify them independently, and read how far the raters agree.

cases.body: Radiographs and CT for one fracture, classified by each rater without seeing the others.

agreement.body: Kappa for each classification system, with its Landis and Koch interpretation.

gold.body: Each rater's accuracy against the reference classification set by the study.

footer.disclaimer: For medical purposes only. Always correlate with clinical findings.

studies.configureGoldStandardInputDesc: Complete the classification questionnaire to set the gold standard. This captures both the classification result and the decision path for divergence analysis.

reliability.fleissKappaDescription: Fleiss' kappa measures agreement among multiple raters across multiple cases. Requires at least 3 raters who completed all cases.
reliability.agreementNote: Agreement percentage shows how often raters selected the same classification for each case. Cases with low agreement (< 60%) are highlighted.

goldStandard.title: Gold standard accuracy
goldStandard.description: Measures how often raters match the expert reference classification. Higher accuracy means raters agree with the gold standard.
goldStandard.noCasesWithGold: No cases in this study have a gold standard set. Set gold standard classifications on individual cases to see accuracy metrics.
goldStandard.casesWithGold: {{count}} of {{total}} cases have a gold standard
goldStandard.hardCasesWarning: {{count}} hard case(s) detected (accuracy < 50% in at least one system)
goldStandard.accuracyNote: Accuracy shows the percentage of raters who matched the gold standard classification. Cases with < 50% accuracy in any system are flagged as hard cases.
goldStandard.raterNote: Shows each rater's accuracy across all gold standard cases in this study. Only cases with a gold standard set are included.

studies.casesLocked: Cases cannot be changed once the study is active or closed.

analytics.distributionDescription: How respondents classified this case across different systems

reliability.title: Inter-rater reliability
reliability.detailedDescription: Confusion matrix and category distribution per classification system
reliability.weightedKappaDescription: Weighted kappa accounts for the severity of disagreements in ordinal classifications. Adjacent category disagreements are penalized less than distant ones.
reliability.diagnosticMetricsDescription: Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values show how well raters identify each classification category compared to the gold standard.
reliability.diagnosticMetricsNote: Values closer to 100% indicate better diagnostic performance. The F1 score is the harmonic mean of sensitivity and PPV, providing a balanced measure of accuracy.
reliability.sensitivityDescription: True positive rate: proportion of actual positives correctly identified (TP / (TP + FN))
reliability.specificityDescription: True negative rate: proportion of actual negatives correctly identified (TN / (TN + FP))
reliability.ppvDescription: Positive predictive value: proportion of positive predictions that are correct (TP / (TP + FP))
reliability.npvDescription: Negative predictive value: proportion of negative predictions that are correct (TN / (TN + FN))
reliability.f1ScoreDescription: Harmonic mean of sensitivity and PPV, providing a balanced measure of accuracy (2 × PPV × sensitivity / (PPV + sensitivity))
reliability.noDataForSystem: No data available for this classification system
reliability.noGoldStandard: No gold standard set for this case
reliability.accuracyDescription: How rater responses compare to the reference classification
reliability.consensusDoesNotMatch: Consensus does not match gold standard
reliability.hardCaseDescription: One or more systems have less than 50% accuracy
reliability.fleissKappaNote: Fleiss' kappa requires multiple cases (subjects) to calculate inter-rater reliability. Current case design has a single case. Consider creating a study with multiple cases for proper reliability assessment.
reliability.kappaLegend: < 0 poor · 0–0.20 slight · 0.21–0.40 fair · 0.41–0.60 moderate · 0.61–0.80 substantial · 0.81–1.00 almost perfect
reliability.kappaNeedsCases: Kappa needs several cases and this is a single case, so percent agreement is shown instead. Group cases in a study to obtain kappa.
